materials.title: A voice chosen for everyone
materials.text:
A spoken guide in a public building (0) IS often heard as the building's own voice. Yet its words are written and selected by particular people. In ____1____ of careful preparation, a guide may leave some visitors feeling that the account has no place for their experience.

The answer is not only to add more voices, ____2____ also to explain how they were chosen. A collection of recordings can sound varied while still reflecting a narrow invitation. No matter ____3____ the final number of contributors is, the process of selecting them remains worth describing.

There is little point ____4____ collecting different accounts if the presentation then removes every difference between them. One speaker may remember a room as welcoming; another may recall being unable to enter. Neither should be made to speak on ____5____ of everyone who used the building.

The editor can preserve disagreement as ____6____ as common ground. That requires enough context for listeners to understand what each account refers to. It is all ____7____ easy to overlook an important part of the story that remains unrecorded.

To some ____8____, every guide offers a route through a larger subject. Its value does not depend on pretending that the route is the territory. Clear information about selection can help visitors enjoy an account while recognising where further questions begin.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 1 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: In spite of forms the concessive expression. In despite of is not the required standard construction.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 2 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: Not only ... but also is the correlative pair. Than is comparative.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 3 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: No matter what the number is forms an embedded variable question. That does not supply the complement value.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 4 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: Little point in collecting uses in plus -ing. To collecting does not fit this construction.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 5 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: On behalf of means representing others. Half does not form this expression.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 6 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: As well as means in addition to. Good does not complete the phrase.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 7 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: All too easy means regrettably easy. To does not complete this degree expression.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 8 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: To some extent/degree qualifies the claim. Amount does not fit the fixed construction.

materials.title: A plan that moved with the timetable
materials.text:
A successful group journey (0) IS sometimes remembered as a sequence in which nothing went wrong. Our trip was not like that. Had it ____1____ been for a railway notice sent the previous evening, we would have arrived at a platform from which no train was leaving.

No sooner had we read the notice ____2____ our organiser began checking alternatives. She did not promise that the original schedule could be preserved. She asked which parts of the visit mattered most and which could move. As long ____3____ we reached the exhibition before its final entry time, the morning's order was flexible.

We contacted the venue by ____4____ of the telephone number on its official booking page. The staff confirmed the entry conditions and advised us which entrance would remain open. That conversation settled a practical question; it did not give us control over the railway.

A few members complained that we should be able to take the advertised train service ____5____ granted. The organiser agreed that reliable information mattered, but said repeating that expectation would not move us towards a working plan. Little ____6____ little, the group stopped comparing every alternative with an impossible original.

____7____ other words, adaptation did not require pretending the disruption was welcome. It required deciding what could still be done. We reached the exhibition with time to look around, rather ____8____ spend the whole morning defending a timetable that no longer applied.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 1 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: Had it not been for is inverted counterfactual condition. No cannot negate been in this construction.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 2 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: No sooner ... than is the comparative temporal pair. Then does not complete the construction.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 3 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: As long as introduces the condition. Than would not form it.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 4 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: By means of names the method. Mean singular is not the fixed expression.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 5 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: Take for granted is the established phrase. As does not fit it.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 6 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: Little by little means gradually. With does not complete the idiom.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 7 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: In other words reformulates the point. On other words does not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 8 with ONE word.
questions.explanation: Rather than contrasts visiting with defending obsolete timetable. Then is temporal, not the conjunction.

materials.title: The island that disappeared
materials.text:
The map in our novel-writing club began as an exercise in (0) IMAGINATION (IMAGINE). Each member added a place before writing a short scene set there. We did not need a real island, but we did need enough ____1____ (PRECISE) for readers to understand how the invented places related to one another.

A river became an immediately ____2____ (RECOGNISE) feature. Different writers used it as a boundary, a route or a source of danger. When a later map omitted a small island at its mouth, several scenes suddenly became difficult to follow.

The island's ____3____ (APPEAR) was accidental. Nobody had intended it to vanish from the story. The artist had simplified the coastline and ____4____ (DELIBERATE) removed minor details, without realising that one apparent detail carried a whole episode.

We restored it and discussed the remaining ____5____ (CERTAIN) about distances. A journey described as a day's walk in one scene took an hour in another. Several ____6____ (COMPARE) between passages revealed that the problem extended beyond the drawing.

It would be a mistake to dismiss the map as ____7____ (RELY) merely because the setting was fictional. It could be consistent or inconsistent with the world the stories established. Its final ____8____ (INTERPRET) depended on those relationships, not on whether the island existed outside the pages. Revising the drawing helped us read the stories more carefully too.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 1 with one word formed from PRECISE.
questions.explanation: Enough precision requires noun. Adjective/adverb do not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 2 with one word formed from RECOGNISE.
questions.explanation: Recognisable/recognizable modifies feature. Noun/adverb do not.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 3 with one word formed from APPEAR.
questions.explanation: Vanish context requires disappearance. Appearance reverses event and appear is verb.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 4 with one word formed from DELIBERATE.
questions.explanation: Deliberately modifies removed. Adjective/noun do not.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 5 with one word formed from CERTAIN.
questions.explanation: Conflicting travel times leave uncertainty, not certainty. Certain adjective does not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 6 with one word formed from COMPARE.
questions.explanation: Several requires plural comparisons. Singular/verb do not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 7 with one word formed from RELY.
questions.explanation: Unreliable is the negative adjective in dismiss as unreliable. The following consistent-or-inconsistent distinction rejects judging reliability merely from fictional status. Reliance noun/reliably adverb do not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 8 with one word formed from INTERPRET.
questions.explanation: Its final interpretation names an act/result of reading. Verb/adjective do not fill noun slot.

materials.title: A meeting with more than one way to speak
materials.text:
The (0) PREPARATION (PREPARE) for our community meeting included a question about participation. The organiser wanted people to be heard without assuming that everyone would respond best to an open invitation to speak before a large group.

All twelve ____1____ (PARTICIPATE) received the main questions in advance. They could prepare a short note or simply think about the topic. Their ____2____ (WILLING) to contribute did not always appear as a hand raised in the first minute.

One member explained that she felt ____3____ (COMFORT) speaking without time to organise her thoughts. She could answer clearly in writing, but became anxious when asked for an immediate response. The organiser changed the format rather than label her uninterested.

Small groups spoke in turn, with time to finish a point without ____4____ (INTERRUPT). Written comments could be submitted ____5____ (ANONYMOUS), although contributors were asked to avoid including other people's private details.

Several ____6____ (SUGGEST) concerned the meeting itself. The organiser kept enough ____7____ (FLEXIBLE) in the schedule to discuss them before returning to the main topic. This did not mean that every proposed change was accepted.

The final plan required ____8____ (COLLABORATE) between people who preferred different ways of working. No single arrangement removed every barrier, but the reasons for the choices were clearer. The meeting's success could not be measured only by counting how many people had spoken aloud.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 1 with one word formed from PARTICIPATE.
questions.explanation: The participants received questions requires plural people. Verb/activity noun do not fit that recipient meaning.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 2 with one word formed from WILLING.
questions.explanation: Their willingness to contribute is noun. Adjective/adverb do not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 3 with one word formed from COMFORT.
questions.explanation: Felt uncomfortable describes anxious state. Comfort noun/uncomfortably adverb do not fit linking felt.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 4 with one word formed from INTERRUPT.
questions.explanation: Without interruption/interruption plural names interruption events. Verb/adjective do not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 5 with one word formed from ANONYMOUS.
questions.explanation: Submitted anonymously requires adverb. Adjective/noun do not modify submission manner.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 6 with one word formed from SUGGEST.
questions.explanation: Several requires plural suggestions. Singular/verb do not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 7 with one word formed from FLEXIBLE.
questions.explanation: Enough flexibility requires noun. Adjective/adverb do not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete gap 8 with one word formed from COLLABORATE.
questions.explanation: Required collaboration names cooperative work. Verb/adjective do not fit.
